rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitmir is the thin membrane around the date stone.
rows.anchor: وهي لفافة النواة، والنقير النقرة في ظهر النواة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqir is the small indentation on the back of the date stone.
rows.anchor: والنقير النقرة في ظهر النواة، والفتيل الذي في وسط النواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatil is the filament in the middle of the date stone.
rows.anchor: والفتيل الذي في وسط النواة. (إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols will say that their worshippers did not worship them, disowning the worship directed to them.
rows.anchor: المعنى يقولون: ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون، فيكفرون بعبادتكم إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expert who informs the Prophet is God, since only God knows and reports what will happen.
rows.anchor: وهو الله، لأن ما أنبأ الله به مما يكون فهو وحده يخبره، لا يشركه فيه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A soul weighed down with sins may call someone to carry its burden, but none of its sins will be carried for it.
rows.anchor: المعنى إن تدع نفس مثقلة بالذنوب إلى حملها، إلى ذنوبها، لا يحمل من ذنوبها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a person called to bear the burden may be a close relative, such as a father or son.
rows.anchor: أي ولو كان الذي تدعوه ذا قربى مثل الأب والابن، ومن أشبه هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet warns all people, but his warning benefits those who fear their Lord.
rows.anchor: والمعنى. ههنا أن إنذارك ينفع الذين يخشون ربهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind person represents an unbeliever blind to truth; the seeing person represents a believer who sees right guidance.
rows.anchor: المعنى لا يستوي الأعمى عن الحق وهو الكافر، والبصير بالحق وهو المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darknesses signify misguidance, while the light signifies guidance.
rows.anchor: ولا الظلمات ولا النور، الظلمات الضلالات، والنور الهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People of truth are in the shade of truth, unlike people of falsehood in lasting heat by night and day.
rows.anchor: لا يستوي أصحاب الحق الذين هم في ظل من الحق، ولا أصحاب الباطل الذين هم في حرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harur is intensely burning heat and its scorching blast, occurring by day and night; samum occurs only by day.
rows.anchor: والحرور استيقاد الحر ولفحه بالنهار وبالليل. والسموم لا يكون إلا بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase introduces the account of the people of the town.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (أصحاب القرية). أي خبر أصحاب القرية

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir identifies the town as Antioch and says Jesus sent two messengers there, whom its people rejected.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنهم أهل إنطاكية، وجه إليهم عيسى اثنين فكذبوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with either gemination or a light consonant.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ فعززنا - بالتشديد والتخفيف - ومعنى فعززنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God strengthened and reinforced the message with a third messenger.
rows.anchor: ومعنى فعززنا فقوينا وشددنا الرسالة بثالث أي برسول ثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers told the people that their duty was only to deliver the message.
rows.anchor: فأعلمهم الرسل إنما عليهم البلاغ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people say that they regard the messengers as an ill omen.
rows.anchor:
قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم)
أي نشاءمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means that they will stone the messengers to death.
rows.anchor:
لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم).
أي لنقتلنكم رجما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression may also be phrased with ṭayr instead of ṭāʾir; he knows of no reader using the shorter form here.
rows.anchor: ويجوز طيركم معكم. لأنه يقال طائر وطير في معنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response means that their ill omen is with them, arising from themselves.
rows.anchor: والمعنى قالوا شؤمكم معكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the people ask whether they become superstitious when reminded.
rows.anchor: أئن ذكرتم). أي أئن ذكرتم تطيرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate reading, aʾan dhukkirtum, means because you were reminded.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ أأن ذكرتم، أي لأن ذكرتم

rows.speaker: أبو زبيد
rows.claim: Abu Zubayd's verse uses lat with awān in a line about a delayed reconciliation.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا لأبي زبيد: طلبوا صلحنا ولات أوان

rows.speaker: أبو العباس محمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas recited Abu Zubayd's line and reported that a kasra variant had also been transmitted.
rows.anchor: والذي أنشدنا أبو العباس محمد بن يزيد ورواه: طلبوا صلحنا ولات أوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative awāna, lat works like laysa; the sense is that this is not the time of escape.
rows.anchor: فأما النصب فعلى أنها عملت عمل ليس، المعنى وليس الوقت حين مناص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative ḥīnu, ḥīn is the subject of laysa and an understood predicate means there is no rescue for us.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع بها جعل حين اسم ليس وأضمر الخبر على معنى ليس حين منجى لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra analysis treats the phrase as an indeclinable form after deleting a genitive complement; Zajjaj calls it anomalous and says Sibawayh and al-Khalil did not transmit it; accusative and nominative are standard.
rows.anchor: ومن خفض جعلها مبينة مكسورة لالتقاء الساكنين، كما قالوا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses lat as la governing an accusative noun, with the tāʾ added as a feminine marker.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: إن (لات حين مناص) نصبها ب (لا) كما تقول لا رجل في الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUjāb means ʿajīb; the form is supported by usage such as karīm and karām for a man.
rows.anchor: في معنى عجيب، ويجوز (عجاب) في معنى عجيب يقال: رجل كريم وكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abu Talib was dying, Quraysh complained of the Prophet; he offered a confession that would win Arab obedience and non-Arab tribute, Abu Jahl mocked the offer, and they left urging one another to cling to their gods.
rows.anchor: هذه حكاية عن ملأ من قريش لما مرض أبو طالب المرضة التي مات فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that the leaders set off saying, “Go on.”
rows.anchor: معناه أي امشوا، وتأويله يقولون امشوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an may be understood as bi-an: they set off with this saying.
rows.anchor: ويجوز: وانطلق الملأ منهم بأن امشوا أي بهذا القول

words: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders claim they had heard nothing like this in Christianity, Judaism, or the tradition they inherited from their fathers.
rows.anchor: أي ما سمعنا بهذا في النصرانية ولا اليهودية ولا فيما أدركنا عليه آباءنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtilāq here means a fabrication or false assertion.
rows.anchor: (إن هذا إلا اختلاق). أي إلا تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection asks how the Quran could have been sent down to Muhammad rather than to someone among them.
rows.anchor: أي كيف أنزل الذكر عليه من بيننا، أي كيف أنزل على محمد القرآن من بيننا

words: بَلْ هُم فِى شَكٍّ مِّن ذِكْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not sincerely believe what they say; they are speaking while in doubt.
rows.anchor: أي ليس يقولون ما يعتقدونه إلا شاكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question links their objections to envy of the Prophet's gift of prophethood: God owns dominion and chooses whom to give kingship, messengership, rain, and mercy.
rows.anchor: فهذا دليل على حسدهم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question's answer is no: the stores of the Lord's mercy do not belong to them.
rows.anchor: (أم عندهم خزائن رحمة ربك). أي ليس عندهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They possess none of the heavens or earth; if they claim otherwise, let them climb the routes that reach heaven.
rows.anchor: أي إن ادعوا شيئا من ذلك فليصعدوا في الأسباب التي توصلهم إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “routes” may instead be the things just mentioned, which only God possesses.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون فليرتقوا في هذه الأسباب التي ذكرت وهي التي لا يملكها إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this challenge, God promises His Prophet victory over the opponents.
rows.anchor: ثم وعد الله نبيه عليه السلام النصر عليهم فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle mā is redundant; the meaning is simply a host there is defeated among the parties.
rows.anchor: لغو، المعنى جند هنالك مهزوم من الأحزاب

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir says Pharaoh had ropes and stakes on which people played for him.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن فرعون كانت له حبال وأوتاد يلعب له عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rooms are elevated dwellings in Paradise, with still higher dwellings above them.
rows.anchor: منازل في الجنة رفيعة، وفوقها منازل أرفع منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading has accusative waʿda as a verbal noun of promise; nominative waʿdu is also allowed, meaning “that is God's promise.”
rows.anchor: القراءة النصب، ويجوز (وعد الله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant's colors include green, yellow, red, white, and other colors.
rows.anchor: ألوانه خضرة وصفرة وحمرة وبياض وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says a plant is described as hāja when it has become fully dry.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي يقال للنبت إذا تم جفافه: قد هاج يهيج هيجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuṭām is plant matter or other material that has crumbled and broken; ruftāt and darīn are comparable terms.
rows.anchor: الحطام ما تفتت وتكسر من النبت وغيره، ومثل الحطام الرفات والدرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene prompts people of understanding to reflect and recognize its evidence for God's oneness.
rows.anchor: أي تفكر لذوي العقول، فيذكرون ما لهم في هذا من الدلالة على توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ marks the result, and the comparison's answer is omitted: one guided by God is unlike one whose heart is sealed and hardened.
rows.anchor: فهذه الفاء فاء المجازاة، والمعنى أفمن شرح الله صدره فاهتدى كمن طبع على قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With min, the phrase means that whenever God's remembrance is recited to them, their hearts become hard, as in the verse about increasing sickness.
rows.anchor: فمن قال من ذكر الله، فالمعنى كلما تلي عليه ذكر الله قسا قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ʿan, the phrase means their hearts have become hard and harsh toward accepting God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: عن ذكر الله فالمعنى أنه غلظ قلبه وجفا عن قبول ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” in manifest error refers to the people whose hearts are hardened.
rows.anchor: أولئك في ضلال مبين). يعني القاسية قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best discourse is the Quran; its passages resemble one another in excellence and wisdom, with no contradiction.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن، ومعنى متشابها، يشابه بعضه بعضا في الفضل والحكمة، لا تناقض فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāban is accusative as a substitute for aḥsan al-ḥadīth.
rows.anchor: و (كتابا) منصوب على البدل من (أحسن الحديث)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathānī is an accusative adjective of kitāban and is diptote because it is a plural not shaped like a singular.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (مثاني) من نعت قوله (كتابا) منصوب على النعت

words: تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When verses of punishment are mentioned, the skins of those who fear God shiver.
rows.anchor: يقول: إذا ذكرت آيات العذاب اقشعرت جلود الخاشعين لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When verses of mercy are mentioned, their skins and hearts soften.
rows.anchor: إذا ذكرت آيات الرحمة لأنت جلودهم وقلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fear of God and His punishment, together with hope for His mercy, is guidance granted by God.
rows.anchor: يقول: الذي وهبه الله لهم من خشيته وخوف عذابه ورجاء رحمته هدي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison omits its answer: the person shielding himself from punishment is unlike the one who enters Paradise.
rows.anchor: هذا مما جوابه محذوف، المعنى كمن يدخل الجنة

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir says the unbeliever is cast into Hell bound and can shield himself from the fire only with his face.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر يلقى في النار مغلولا، لا يتهيأ له أن يتقي النار إلا بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalnāhu means that God gave him the blessing as a favor; any gift given without compensation is called a bestowal.
rows.anchor: أعطيناه ذلك تفضلا، وكل من أعطى على غير جزاء فقد خول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipient claims that his distinction and merit entitle him to the gift and that he knew he would receive it.
rows.anchor: أي أعطيته على شرف وفضل يجب له به هذا الذي أعطيت، فقد علمت أني ساعطى هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says the gift is a trial and test, by which the servant is tested to see whether he gives thanks or disbelieves.
rows.anchor: أي تلك العطية فتنة من الله وبلوى يبتلى بها العبد ليشكر أو يكفر

words: فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the earlier people had earned did not benefit them because their works were nullified.
rows.anchor: يقول: فأحبطت أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return is to God, who will repay them for their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي إلى الله مرجعهم فيجازيهم بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qanata means to despair; the command not to despair means not to lose hope.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (لا تقنطوا) لا تيأسوا

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Tafsir reports that people in Mecca thought idolatry, associating partners with God, and murder were unforgivable; God declares that anyone who repents and believes can be forgiven all sins.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن قوما من أهل مكة قالوا إن محمدا يقول: إن من عبد الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anībū means repent.
rows.anchor: وأسلموا له من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب ثم لا تنصرون (54)

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: A second reported occasion is people in Mecca who were tempted and tortured over their religion, then left Islam; God says that if they repent and return to Islam, He will forgive them.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها نزلت في قوم فتنوا، في دينهم، وعذبوا يمكة فرجعوا عن الإسلام

words: أَحْسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best thing sent down is the Quran, as shown by the earlier description of it as the best discourse.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن ودليله: (الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها)

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iraqi codices have aw an yuẓhira; the Hijazi codex has wa-an yuẓhira without the alif, and the latter form is also allowed.
rows.anchor: على هذا مصاحف أهل العراق، وفي مصحف أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With aw, Pharaoh presents alternatives: he fears Moses will abolish the religion, or, if not abolish it, corrupt it; Pharaoh calls obedience to God corruption.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أو وقوع أحد الشيئيق فالمعنى على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With wa-an, Pharaoh claims to fear that the religion will be abolished and corruption will come with it.
rows.anchor: فيكون المعنى أخاف إبطال دينكم والفساد معه

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: One report in tafsir names the believing man of Pharaoh's household Samʿān.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن هذا الرجل أعني مؤمن آل فرعون، كان أن يسمى سمعان

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Another reported view gives the man's name as Habib.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان اسمه حبيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes “from Pharaoh's household” an adjective of man and supplies minhum with “concealing his faith,” meaning he hid it from them.
rows.anchor: ويكون (من آل فرعون) صفة للرجل

words: رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَٰنَهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “concealing his faith” modifies “man”: he was a believer from Pharaoh's household who concealed his faith.
rows.anchor: ويكون يكتم من صفة رجل، فيكون المعنى: وقال رجل مؤمن يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause means “because he says, My Lord is God.”
rows.anchor: المعنى لأن يقول ربي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear signs are signs of prophethood that demonstrate the man's truthfulness.
rows.anchor: أي بما يدل على صدقه من آيات النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the man is lying, the lie harms him and does not harm his opponents.
rows.anchor: فعليه كذبه) أي فلا يضركم

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a Prophet's full promise comes to pass, saying “some” imposes the argument with its easiest consequence; it does not deny that all of it will occur.
rows.anchor: وهذا من لطيف المسائل، لأن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إذا وعد وعدا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses “some of his need” to illustrate the use of “some” as the easiest part of an argument.
rows.anchor:
ومثل هذا قول الشاعر:
قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding creation account places its creation on Monday.
rows.anchor: خلقها في يوم الاثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains and provisions were made on Tuesday and Wednesday, completing four days in all.
rows.anchor: في الثلاثاء والأربعاء فصارت الجملة أربعة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With genitive sawāʾ, it modifies the days: the four days are equal or complete.
rows.anchor: فمن خفض جعله صفة للأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With accusative sawāʾ, it is a verbal noun meaning that the days were made even or complete.
rows.anchor: على معنى استوت سواء، واستواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With nominative sawāʾ, it is a predicate: they are equal or complete.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع فعلى معنى هي سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For those who ask” can attach to the statement that God apportioned provisions, meaning for everyone needing sustenance.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (للسائلين)، معلق بقوله: (وقدر فيها أقواتها) لكل محتاج إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase addresses people asking how long creation took: the earth was made in four days, with no more or less.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون للسائلين لمن سأل في كم خلقت السماوات والأرضون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawā ilā means that God turned or directed Himself toward heaven.
rows.anchor: معنى استوى عمد إلى السماء وقصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāʾiʿīn is an accusative circumstantial expression; heaven and earth are treated like rational beings, explaining the masculine plural.
rows.anchor: على الحال منصوب، وإنما قيل طائعين دون طائعات، لأنهن جرين مجرى ما يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the words mean “we and those within us came obediently.”
rows.anchor: وقد قيل (قالتا أتينا) أي، نحن ومن فينا طائعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to obey willingly or to be compelled to obey.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة أطيعا الطاعة أو تكرها إكراها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-qaḍāhunna means that God created and fashioned the seven heavens.
rows.anchor:
(فقضاهن). فخلقهن وصنعهن.
قال أبو ذؤيب

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb's poem uses qaḍāhumā to mean that the two garments were made or fashioned.
rows.anchor:
قال أبو ذؤيب.
وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: One reported interpretation says God assigned each heaven what would sustain or suit it.
rows.anchor: أوحى في كل سماء أمرها). قيل ما يصلحها

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the matter assigned to each heaven to mean its angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل ملائكتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lamps are also a protection against devils listening in; the stars preserve the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: معناه وحفظناها من استماع الشياطين بالكواكب حفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night, day, sun, and moon are signs that show God is one.
rows.anchor: أي من علاماته التي تدل على أنه واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun may refer to non-rational plurals, which take feminine agreement; a masculine plural pronoun is reserved for rational beings.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أن ضمير غير ما يعقل على لفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the feminine pronoun refers to the implied feminine plural āyāt, since the listed objects are called God's signs.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون (خلقهن) راجعا على معنى الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Muhammad; if the opponents refuse God's oneness, worship, and belief in His messenger, the angels glorify Him day and night without tiring.
rows.anchor: هذه خطاب لمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not grow weary.
rows.anchor:
لا يسأمون).
لا يملون - ثم زادهم في الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is crumbling and changed, like hāmida.
rows.anchor: أي متهشمة متغيرة، وهو مثل هامدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with hamza as rabaʾat.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ وربأت بالهمز، ومعنى ربت عظمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabat means grew or swelled, while rabaʾat means rose as the ground lifts when plants are about to emerge.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ربت عظمت، ومعنى ربأت ارتفعت لأن النبت إذا هم أن يظهر ارتفعت له الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with fatḥa on both the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ.
rows.anchor: (يلحدون) بفتح الياء والحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād means to divert speech from its proper direction; laḥada and alḥada have the same meaning, like digging a grave to one side.
rows.anchor: وتفسير يلحدون يجعلون الكلام على غير جهته، ومن هذا اللحد لأنه الحفر في جانب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased as an imperative, this is a threat and warning; the promised recompense has already been made clear.
rows.anchor: لفط هذا الكلام لفظ أمر، ومعناه الوعيد والتهدد، وقد بين لهم المجازاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yastajību means that God answers those who believe and do good works.
rows.anchor: المعنى ويجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun may be either accusative or nominative; on the accusative parsing, the sense is that God answers the believers.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون نصبا، ويجوز أن يكون رفعا. فمن نصب فعلى معنى ويجيب الله الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaniṭū is also read with kasra on the nūn; both qaniṭa yaqniṭu and qanaṭa yaqnaṭu mean to despair.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ (قنطوا) بكسر النون، يقال قنط يقنط

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When Umar was told the land had become barren and people had despaired, he replied that rain would come, invoking this verse.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن عمر قيل له قد أجدبت الأرض وقنط الناس فقال: مطروا إذن، لهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan codices omit the fāʾ, except in Abu Jaʿfar's reading; Iraqi codices and readers include it, which is better Arabic because the fāʾ answers the conditional.
rows.anchor: في مصحف أهل المدينة (بما كسبت أيديكم) - بغير فاء -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading has an implied an because a conditional precedes it; it may also be nominative as a new clause or jussive.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (ويعلم الذين يجادلون) والنصب على إضمار أن

rows.speaker: علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports from the Prophet that God is too generous to punish a servant twice: one punished by a worldly affliction for his deeds is not punished again in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading without fāʾ, God does not requite people in this world for much of what they have earned.
rows.anchor: أي لا يجازى على كثير مما كسبت أيديكم قي الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that God does not requite much of what they have earned either in this world or the next.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون (يعفو عن كثير) فلا يجازى عليه في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maḥīṣ means a way out or refuge; ḥāṣa and ḥāḍa can both mean to turn aside.
rows.anchor: ما لهم من معدل، ولا من منجى، يقال حاص عنه إذا تنحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although it would have the same meaning, the word may not be read with ḍād as maḥīḍ.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يقرأ ما لهم من محيض، وأن كان المعنى واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb faʿtilūhu is read with either ḍamma or kasra on its tāʾ.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ فاعتلوه - بضم التاء وكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is addressed to the angels and means to seize him and drag him away roughly and forcefully.
rows.anchor: المعنى يا أيها الملائكة خذوه فاعتلوه. والعتل أن يؤخذ فيمضى به بعسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-jaḥīm means the middle of Hell.
rows.anchor: إلى سواء الجحيم) إلى وسط الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers except al-Kisaʾi read inna with kasra; al-Kisaʾi reads anna with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: الناس كلهم على كسر " إنك " إلا الكسائي وحده فإنه قرأ: ذق أنك

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: On al-Kisaʾi's reading, the condemned man is told to taste punishment because he had boasted that he was the mightiest and most protected man in the valley.
rows.anchor: إلا الكسائي وحده فإنه قرأ: ذق أنك أنت، أي لأنك قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise are secure from others there.
rows.anchor: أي قد أمنوا فيه الغير

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The reported interpretation identifies istabraq as thick brocade.
rows.anchor: قيل الإستبرق: الديباج الصفيق (2). والسندس: الحرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is silk; istabraq may be named for its intense sheen.
rows.anchor: والسندس: الحرير، وإنما قيل له إستبرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular of amʿāʾ is miʿā, with a plural pattern like ḍilʿ and aḍlāʿ.
rows.anchor: واحد الأمعاء معى، مثل ضلع وأضلاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who listen to the Prophet and then ask what he said are hypocrites.
rows.anchor: يعني المنافقين. (حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك

words: قَالُوا۟ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ مَاذَا قَالَ ءَانِفًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They listened to the Prophet's sermon, then asked the Companions what he had just said in mockery and to show they had paid no attention.
rows.anchor: كانوا يسمعون خطبة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فإذا خرجوا سألوا أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānifan means just now or at the near beginning; the word relates to beginning something anew and to a pasture not yet grazed.
rows.anchor: أي ماذا قال الساعة، ومعنى آنفا من قولك استأنفت الشيء إذا ابتدأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred referent of the pronoun in “increased them” is God, so He is the one increasing the guided in guidance.
rows.anchor: فأجودها - والله أعلم - أن يكون فيه ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to the Messenger: what he said increased the guided in guidance.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير في (زادهم) قول الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that the hypocrites' turning away and mockery increased the guided in guidance.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون زادهم إعراض المنافقين واستهزاؤهم هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ātāhum taqwāhum may mean that God inspired them with piety, as in the verse about being made to hold fast to the word of piety.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون وألهمهم تقواهم، كما قال عز وجل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means that God gave them the reward for their piety.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون - والله أعلم - وآتاهم ثواب تقواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate reading has in taʾtihim without the yāʾ; the form matching the muṣḥaf is better.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ " إلا الساعة إن تأتهم " بغير ياء، والأولى أجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause an taʾtiya is an accusative apposition to al-sāʿa, meaning they await only the Hour's sudden arrival.
rows.anchor: وموضع " أن " نصب البدل من الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apposition includes the earlier noun in meaning.
rows.anchor: وهذا البدل المشتمل على الأول في المعنى وهو نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Backbiting is speaking ill of an absent person, even when what is said about the person is true.
rows.anchor: والغيبة أن يذكر الإنسان من خلفه بسوء وإن كان فيه السوء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited for the distinction: speaking ill of an absent person with a true description is backbiting, while attributing something untrue is slander.
rows.anchor: وأما ذكره بما ليس فيه فذلك البهت والبهتان - كذلك جاء عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

words: أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form may also be read as mayyitan.
rows.anchor: ويجوز (ميتا) وتأويله أن ذكرك بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking ill of an absent person is like eating his dead flesh, since he cannot feel it; people also say a backbiter eats people's flesh.
rows.anchor: وتأويله أن ذكرك بسوء من لم يحضر لك بمنزلة أكل لحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as people hate eating a dead brother's flesh, they should avoid speaking ill of someone who is absent.
rows.anchor: فتأويله كما تكرهون أكل لحمه ميتا كذلك تجنبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people descend from Adam and Eve and share one father and one mother.
rows.anchor: خلقناكم من آدم وحواء، وكلكم بنو أب واحد وأم واحدة إليهما ترجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A shaʿb is larger than a tribe.
rows.anchor: والشعب أعظم من القبيلة. أي لم يجعلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made people into peoples and tribes so that they would recognize one another, not boast over one another.
rows.anchor: أي لم يجعلكم شعوبا وقبائل لتفاخروا وإنما جعلناكم كذلك لتتعارفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest rank with God belongs to the most pious.
rows.anchor: ثم أعلمهم الله - عز وجل - أن أرفعهم عنده منزلة أتقاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may also be read with anna, yielding the sense that God made people tribes so they might know one another, that the most noble before God is the most pious.
rows.anchor: ولو قرئت " أن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم " جاز ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam is outward submission and acceptance of the Prophet's message, which protects a person's blood; when joined with inward belief and assent, the person is truly both Muslim and believer, without doubt.
rows.anchor: والإسلام إظهار الخضوع والقبول لما أتى به النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وبذلك يحقن الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true believer accepts that religious obligations and jihad with his person and wealth are binding, without doubt.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي يرى أن أداء الفرائض واجب عليه، وأن الجهاد بنفسه وماله واجب عليه لا يدخله في ذلك ريب
